claims.text: Inducing coherent nanoprecipitates in a refractory high-entropy alloy improves high-temperature mechanical strength relative to a homogeneous single-phase alloy.
Inducing coherent nanoprecipitates improves high-temperature thermoelastic stability relative to a homogeneous single-phase alloy.
Coherent nanoprecipitates facilitate smoother dislocation motion.
A tailored aging or heat-treatment cycle can form stepwise-controllable coherent nanoprecipitates in the refractory high-entropy alloy.
The proposed behavior is applicable from room temperature to approximately 900 °C.
Nanoprecipitates and their interfaces relieve local stress concentrations.
Nanoprecipitates and their interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission through the microstructure.
Nanoprecipitates serve as barriers to lattice diffusion.
The combined dislocation and diffusion effects of the nanoprecipitates reduce creep rate.
The combined dislocation and diffusion effects reduce thermal softening and maintain high-temperature strength.
The nanoprecipitate-containing alloy will have higher yield strength than the homogeneous baseline alloy.
The nanoprecipitate-containing alloy will have greater ductility than the homogeneous baseline alloy.
The nanoprecipitate-containing alloy will have a lower creep rate than the homogeneous baseline alloy.
The nanoprecipitate-containing alloy will retain a more stable thermoelastic modulus than the homogeneous baseline alloy.
The beneficial effects may diminish when nanoprecipitate size or distribution is inadequately controlled.
Nanoprecipitate size, volume fraction, and spatial distribution influence the magnitude of the mechanical-property changes.
A same-composition comparison with identical high-temperature loading and verified precipitate versus homogeneous microstructures can test the proposed causal effect.
